songs.name: Sittin' On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Ripping rockers and psychedelic suite, tape hiss fades later
ai_show_review.blurb: The set launches with a scorching “Hard To Handle” and a tight “Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > High Time” triptych. Jerry’s guitar work shines, Tom Constanten adds a memorable touch on “Casey Jones”, and the band wraps up with a powerful “Saint Stephen – Turn On Your Lovelight”. Recording is clear early on but deteriorates after the mid‑set.
ai_show_review.review: July 4 1969 at Chicago’s Electric Theater captures the Dead in a raw, transitional phase. The night opens with the high‑octane swagger of “Hard To Handle” and rolls into the cryptic, weaving jam of “Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > High Time”, where Jerry Garcia not only delivers his signature ripping leads but even slips on pedal steel and a brief vocal stumble (“swallowed a frog”). Bob Weir fronts several numbers, from the country‑flavored “Mama Tried” to the bluesy “Dire Wolf”. Tom Constanten’s keyboard colors shine on “Casey Jones”, providing one of the few clear moments in an otherwise uneven recording. The set closes with a soaring “Saint Stephen – Turn On Your Lovelight”, showcasing the band’s ability to swing between psychedelic intensity and soulful groove. Unfortunately, both available tapes suffer: the audience stereo (gd69-07-04.sbd.sirmick.remaster.29294.shnf) loses fidelity after “Doin' That Rag” with hiss and drop‑outs, while the soundboard source (gd69-07-04.sbd.cotsman.4360.sbeok.shnf) is plagued by pervasive tape noise and splices, making only “Casey Jones” truly listenable. Despite these flaws, the performance offers a fascinating glimpse of the band’s evolving repertoire and on‑stage chemistry.

best_recording.reason: Early stereo audience tape is clear and well‑balanced, preserving the strongest part of the show before later hiss and drop‑outs make it harder to enjoy.

key_highlights: Fire‑brand “Hard To Handle” opener with Garcia’s ripping guitar.
"Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > High Time" suite showcases psychedelic improvisation.
Tom Constanten’s memorable keyboard work on "Casey Jones".
"Saint Stephen – Turn On Your Lovelight" delivers a powerful closing jam.

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers ripping guitar work, adds pedal steel on several cuts, and has a brief vocal stumble during High Time.
band_performance.Bob: Front‑and‑center vocalist on many numbers, including Dire Wolf and the cowboy‑flavored tunes.
